methodological_rigor.justification: TRIDENT-1 is a single-arm registrational phase 1/2 multicenter trial in 152 sites across 19 countries with 120 efficacy-evaluable NTRK+ patients in two cohorts (TKI-naive n=51, TKI-pretreated n=69) and 565 safety-population patients. Prespecified primary endpoint is BICR-assessed confirmed objective response per RECIST v1.1 with mRECIST for intracranial disease. Design is robust for a rare-disease tumor-agnostic trial; limitations (single-arm, small sample size, NSCLC predominance) are acknowledged. The prespecified TKI-naive target of 55 was not met (enrolled 51).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Repotrectinib is approved for NTRK+ solid tumors and for ROS1+ NSCLC and is now listed in NCCN guidelines across multiple tumor types. This trial provides the first efficacy data in a TKI-pretreated NTRK+ population with solvent-front mutations (53% response rate), directly informing sequencing after larotrectinib/entrectinib failure, and documents durable intracranial activity. Single-arm, basket-design phase 1/2 -> Oxford LoE 2b (prospective non-randomized cohort-equivalent).

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript includes a CONSORT diagram (Fig 1), detailed endpoint definitions, BICR adjudication, CTCAE v4.03 grading, explicit statistical plan with Clopper-Pearson CIs, Kaplan-Meier methods, and Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary. Data and code availability statements are referenced as online but text not visible in normalized file. Standard is CONSORT (single-arm trial); a fully CONSORT-aligned extension for non-randomized studies (TREND) could be more precise, but CONSORT is the closest applicable.

novelty_literature.justification: First trial to report efficacy of a next-generation TRK TKI in a TKI-pretreated NTRK+ solid-tumor population, including activity against solvent-front mutations (53% ORR). It extends larotrectinib/entrectinib landscape by addressing acquired resistance and intracranial disease. Not a first-in-class discovery (tumor-agnostic TRK inhibition precedent exists), but fills a clearly defined clinical gap for post-TKI patients.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear Nature-style structure with Main, Methods, Results, and Discussion; efficacy outcomes reported separately for TKI-naive and TKI-pretreated cohorts with CIs; intracranial activity, solvent front mutations, and resistance analyses are each discussed. Limitations (single-arm, small NTRK+ sample) are explicitly stated. Figures/tables and supplementary material are appropriately signposted.

key_strengths: Registrational phase 1/2 basket trial supporting FDA approval of repotrectinib in NTRK+ solid tumors
BICR-confirmed ORR in TKI-naive (59%) and TKI-pretreated (48%) cohorts, with 53% ORR in solvent front mutations
Durable responses: median DOR NE in TKI-naive (85% at >=24 months) and 9.8 months in pretreated
Intracranial activity with no new brain lesions in patients without baseline intracranial disease (TKI-naive)
Large safety database (n=565) with low rate of TRAE-related discontinuation (4%)
key_concerns: Single-arm design precludes direct comparison with larotrectinib/entrectinib
Prespecified TKI-naive cohort target (55) not reached (51 evaluable)
OS immature in TKI-naive cohort; cross-trial comparisons to other TRK TKIs inherently biased
Data/code availability referenced to online, not visible in normalized text
chief_reviewer.rationale: Registrational phase 1/2 data with practice-informing findings in a rare molecular subgroup, including novel evidence of activity against on-target resistance mutations; appropriately positioned at Tier 1 oncology (e.g., Nature Medicine/Lancet Oncology).
